column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
FELIX_HARNESS_DIR holds lib/maintenance.sh, so it is an engine harness
a FELIX_HARNESS_DIR inherited from the caller is replaced by the lib's own
a bare commit is not a remote-tracking ref: exit 2, one line
a bound of 0 is no bound
a bound of 5000 seconds keeps only the fold whose tip is 2730 seconds old
a branch pruned after it was listed does not blank the read: main is still read, the live fold still named
a branch that only adds a pending file, its marker equal to main's, is not in flight
a branch under another remote is not counted for origin/main
a branch whose HANDOFF.md has no marker is not in flight
a branch whose first marker is main's is not in flight, whatever id it quotes lower down
a branch whose marker is behind main's, though cut from main's tip, is not in flight
a branch with no HANDOFF.md is not in flight
a check that exits 0 naming one holder is inflight, holder in field 3
a fold cut from an older main whose handoff has since moved is stale, not in flight
a fold main has already taken (its tip is in main, its marker is main's) is not in flight
a holder keeps its text and drops its control bytes
a holder printed with no trailing newline still counts
a local branch (refs/heads) is never counted, though it holds a live fold
a local branch is not a remote-tracking ref, though it holds main's commit: exit 2, one line
a ref that does not resolve cannot be examined: exit 2, one line on stdout
a ref whose HANDOFF.md has no marker cannot be examined: exit 2, one line
a ref with no HANDOFF.md cannot be examined: exit 2, one line
a symbolic ref such as origin/HEAD is never counted, even when it points at a fold in flight
an inflight row is not rendered as a passed check
and due because the script answered none in flight (exit 1), not because it could not run
and exits 0 on it called by a relative path from a subdirectory, finding its library from where it was called
and it is named however git orders its merge-bases, since every base is read
and keeps the row's description there
and names the holders: on <holders>
and says in flight on that row
and says it once, on a line of its own
and says the same called by a relative path from a subdirectory, finding its libraries from where it was called
and says the same called by a relative path from a subdirectory, finding its library from where it was called
and that row reads inflight, since the check printed it and exited 0
and the emitted inflight row keeps exactly five fields
and the line names it
and the row's reason is given
and the script says it is dated ahead, rather than 0m old
and the script says none in flight for it (exit 1)
and the script says none in flight for them (exit 1)
and the shim did prune it, so the line above read the race
and the third field is the tip's committer time in Unix seconds
bin/handoff-in-flight, run from a subdirectory with no arguments, reads origin/main within 48 hours and names each fold, newest first, exit 0
blank lines, leading, inner and trailing, are dropped from the holders
each id is the branch's current id from its first marker, not a phrase quoted lower down
each inflight row adds a line of its own
every tab inside a holder line becomes a space
felix maintenance marks the row in-flt
felix_handoff_in_flight names every fold in flight on origin, one <branch> <id> <epoch> line each, newest tip first, and exits 0
fold order: 0aaa is after 0zz, though it sorts before it as a string
fold order: 0da is after 0cz, so a fold to 0da from a main at 0cz is in flight
fold order: 0zz is before 0aaa, though it sorts after it as a string, so it is not in flight
folds are ordered by tip time, newest first, not by name or by id
given a bound of 48 hours in seconds, a fold whose tip is 72 hours old is left out
handoff-in-flight --within 0 is no bound, and a tip 72 hours old is said in hours
handoff-in-flight --within 1.5 exits 2, since hours are whole
handoff-in-flight --within 100 is a hundred hours, so the 72-hour tip is named
handoff-in-flight --within 3 is three hours: the 5-hour and 72-hour tips are left out
handoff-in-flight --within abc exits 2: cannot examine
handoff-in-flight --within with no value exits 2
handoff-in-flight answers from git alone and never runs gh
handoff-in-flight on a local branch exits 2: not a remote-tracking ref
handoff-in-flight on a ref that does not resolve exits 2: cannot examine
handoff-in-flight on a ref with no marker exits 2: cannot examine
handoff-in-flight outside any checkout exits 2, since origin/main does not resolve
handoff-in-flight takes the ref as its argument, the short form included
handoff-in-flight with an unknown option exits 2
handoff-in-flight with nothing in flight exits 1 and prints nothing, as grep does
it examines the checkout it is given as <root>, from any working directory
it reads the folds in flight from git alone and never runs gh
naming the second row with its own holder
on the line directly under the in-flt row
once the fold is on the remote the row is inflight, naming the branch, its id and its age
only stdout names holders; what the check said on stderr is not one
only the inflight row is marked in-flt, not the silent ok row
session start names the holder: 'Already in flight, so not due: <name> on <holders>'
sourced from another harness, FELIX_HARNESS_DIR names that harness instead
the age is whole minutes under an hour and whole hours otherwise, rounded down: 0m 1m 45m 59m 1h 2h 72h
the branch is named under the remote, without origin/ or refs/remotes/
the check runs in the checkout root it was given
the check runs with FELIX_HARNESS_DIR set to the harness the lib was sourced from
the founder's case 10: a here-document a shell reads is its script
the founder's case 11: and so with -s
the founder's case 12: a redirect's target is written whatever line the here-document ends on
the founder's case 1: a separator glued to the last word ends it, as the shell does
the founder's case 2: a group's separator ends the word too
the founder's case 3: a line break ends a word as a blank does
the founder's case 4: a shell's -c script is a command of its own, quotes and all
the founder's case 5: and so under bash -c
the founder's case 6: a -c script handed to find's -exec is still a command
the founder's case 7: a $( ) assigned to a variable runs
the founder's case 8: a quoted program name is the program
the founder's case 9: a quoted path in command position runs
the in-flight line appears when nothing is due
the reader prints a command separator as a token of its own, an operator of two characters whole
the short form origin/main is read as refs/remotes/origin/main
two non-empty lines are joined by '; ', in the order printed
with no bound it is named
with nothing in flight it prints nothing and exits 0
with only inflight, ok, event and dormant rows, felix maintenance shows the inflight row
